text: Merge sort with inversion counting; a^b in O(log b).

Divide and conquer (分治): split the problem into halves, solve each half recursively, then combine the two answers. If combining costs O(n), the whole thing costs O(n log n): there are log n levels, each doing O(n) work.
Merge sort is the model: sort both halves, then merge two sorted lists. Anything that can be counted while merging, such as inversions, comes for free.

When a[j] from the right half is placed before a[i] from the left half, it is smaller than every remaining a[i..m]: that is m − i + 1 inversions at once (P1908). Use long long : n = 5 × 10⁵ can give 1.25 × 10¹¹ inversions. Two rows of matches need as many adjacent swaps as there are inversions after matching ranks (P1966).
square a each step, multiply in when the bit is 1
ab by multiplying b times is O(b), hopeless for b = 10⁹. Write b in binary: ab is the product of a2ᵏ over the 1-bits of b, and a2ᵏ comes from squaring. O(log b) multiplications (P1226).

Take % p after every multiplication, and keep values in long long so a product of two numbers below p (up to about 3 × 10⁹) fits. Start from 1 % p , so p = 1 gives 0. With big numbers instead of mod, the same loop computes 2ᴾ (P1045).
Answers left, right, or crossing the middle; closest pair of points.

Many sequence problems split the same way: the answer lies entirely in the left half, entirely in the right half, or crosses the middle. Recursion handles the first two; only the crossing case needs new code, and it usually has a simple shape because it must touch the middle.

A crossing subarray = (best sum ending at m, going left) + (best sum starting at m + 1, going right). Two linear scans per level: O(n log n). The O(n) method of 第1章 is faster, but this pattern carries over to problems that have no simple scan (P1115).

Closest pair of points: after solving both halves with best distance d, a crossing pair must lie within d of the dividing line, and sorted by y each point only needs to be compared with the next few points closer than d vertically: O(n log² n) (P1257). Sums over all pairs such as MooFest (P2345) are also counted across the middle while merging.
Sparse tables for O(1) range max/min; jumping 2ᵏ steps.
length 2 blocks length 4 blocks

Binary lifting (倍增): precompute the answer for blocks of length 1, 2, 4, 8, …; any length is a sum of powers of two, so a few precomputed blocks cover it. A sparse table (ST 表) stores mx[k][i] = max of a[i … i + 2ᵏ − 1].

A range max/min query [l, r] is covered by two overlapping blocks of length 2ᵏ, with k = ⌊log₂(r − l + 1)⌋: one starting at l, one ending at r. Overlap is harmless for max and min, so each query is O(1) after O(n log n) preparation.

A block of length 2ᵏ is two blocks of length 2ᵏ⁻¹, so each table row comes from the row before. The tallest minus the shortest cow in a range (P2880) and the most loyal (smallest) account in a range (P1816) are direct ST-table queries. Sums do not work with overlapping blocks; use prefix sums for those.

When every position has exactly one "next" position, 2ᵏ steps = two jumps of 2ᵏ⁻¹ steps. With the table, t steps (even t = 10¹²) take one jump per 1-bit of t: O(log t) per query, the same binary idea as fast power.

Water falling through fountains (P7167), the fewest guards to cover a circle (P4155) and frogs jumping k times (P3509) all build such a jump table and then jump by powers of two. In 第9章 the same table finds lowest common ancestors in trees.
The Luogu problems for this chapter, a ladder through them, and experiments to try yourself.
Key points to memorise
1. Divide and conquer: split, solve halves, combine; O(n) combine → O(n log n).
2. Inversions: while merging, taking a[j] from the right adds m − i + 1; use long long.
3. Fast power: if (b & 1) res = res·a % p; a = a·a % p; b >>= 1.
4. Start from 1 % p; mod after every multiplication.
5. Crossing case: best ending at m (going left) + best starting at m + 1.
6. Closest pair: strip of width d around the middle, sorted by y, few checks per point.
7. ST table: mx[k][i] from two halves of length 2ᵏ⁻¹; query with k = log₂(len), two overlapping blocks.
8. Overlap is fine for max/min/gcd, not for sums.
9. Jump table: nxt[k][i] = nxt[k−1][nxt[k−1][i]]; jump by the 1-bits of t.
